data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet summarizes Czechia’s performance on the PISA Creative Thinking cognitive test for 15-year-old students. The test measures three ideation processes—generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, and evaluating and improving ideas—across four domain contexts: written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, and scientific problem solving. Czechia’s mean creative thinking score is 33 out of 60, which is on par with the OECD average, and the relative performance aligns with expectations based on mathematics and reading performance. The factsheet reports that 80% of students reach at least Level 3, while 25% are top performers at Levels 5–6. It also highlights within-country gaps: socio-economic status predicts creative thinking (explaining 15% of variation in Czechia), girls outperform boys by 2.9 points, and several creativity-related beliefs and school environment indicators are associated with higher performance. The document is descriptive and does not provide ML model metrics or methodological details on PV/missing-data handling at the factsheet level.
